To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) users are able to identify the relevant attributes of an image classification model, (ii) concept-based explanations do not help users to identify relevant attributes, and (iii) counterfactual explanations are not better at identifying relevant attributes than a baseline.

1) a simple baseline explanation outperforms concept-based explanations, 2) users can identify the relevant attribute set for a given image, 3) users are able to identify the correct attribute set for counterfactual explanations, and 4) users benefit from the explanations in a user study, but only to a limited extent.
